components.css: .ds-pad { position: relative; width: 360px; aspect-ratio: 3/2; padding: 3px; border-radius: 22px; background: linear-gradient(to bottom, #1e1d20, #18171a); box-shadow: 0 1px 0 0 rgba(255,250,240,0.07) inset, 0 -1px 0 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.5) inset, 0 22px 48px -24px rgba(0,0,0,0.9); } .ds-face { position: absolute; inset: 3px; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 19px; background: #141315; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.55) inset; } .ds-zone { position: absolute; width: 31%; height: 50%; padding: 12px; box-sizing: border-box; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; transition: background-color 200ms; } .ds-top { top: 0; } .ds-bot { bottom: 0; } .ds-l { left: 0; align-items: flex-start; background: linear-gradient(to right, oklch(0.76 var(--c) var(--h) / 0.24), oklch(0.76 var(--c) var(--h) / 0.07), transparent); } .ds-r { right: 0; align-items: flex-end; text-align: right; background: linear-gradient(to left, oklch(0.76 var(--c) var(--h) / 0.24), oklch(0.76 var(--c) var(--h) / 0.07), transparent); } .ds-zone:hover { background: oklch(0.76 var(--c) var(--h) / 0.14); } .ds-zname { font: 400 11px Inter, sans-serif; color: #9e9891; } .ds-act { margin-top: auto; font: 600 14px Inter, sans-serif; color: #fffdf9; } .ds-key { font: 400 11px 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; color: #9e9891; } .ds-center { position: absolute; left: 33%; right: 33%; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); text-align: center; font: 600 13px 'Sora Variable', Sora, Inter, sans-serif; color: oklch(0.86 calc(var(--c) * 0.7) var(--h)); }

narrative.overview:
Noma wears the colour of the app you're in. The window frame, the wash at the top of every page, the app's own name and the trackpad's zones all take the current app's hue, the way an Arc space or a Things area has its own colour. Switch from VS Code to Spotify and the colour slides across the window over 700ms. You know whose four actions you're looking at before you read a word.

Everything else stays out of the way: a warm graphite ground (brown-black, never blue-black), off-white ink for the one thing you press, Sora for titles, Inter for reading, JetBrains Mono only for keys and shortcuts. Surfaces are solid materials with real offset shadows: no glass, no glow, no colour on cards. Flow, the part of Noma that notices repeated work, speaks on its own violet paper, so a suggestion never reads as part of the interface. Gold appears only when real hardware is in contact.

The system replaces the earlier one-accent (blue `#4c7eff`) "frosted metal and glass" dashboard. It refuses that pattern specifically: no single brand accent on every control, no uppercase eyebrow labels over sections, no AI gradients or glow, no fake 3D hardware.
keyCharacteristics: One colour per app (OKLCH hue + chroma, fixed lightness), meaning only "where you are".
Off-white ink is the only "press me" colour; one primary per view.
Warm graphite ground in six steps; warm neutral text in seven.
Real offset shadows plus a hairline inset top-light on every raised surface.
Sora sentence-case titles; no kickers; mono only for keys.
The trackpad is the signature object, drawn at one scale everywhere.

rules.name: The Where-You-Are Rule
rules.body: The app's colour means only "where you are": the frame, the page wash, the app's name, its zones and its icon plate. Never a button, a chart series, a status, or decoration. If removing the hue would lose information about which app this is, it belongs; otherwise it doesn't.

rules.name: The Ink Rule
rules.body: Off-white ink is the only "press me" colour, and a view has at most one ink button. Everything else is a raised graphite key or a quiet text action.

rules.name: The Flow's Voice Rule
rules.body: Violet is Flow speaking: a suggestion, something Flow noticed. Never general UI, never a highlight.

rules.name: The Real Contact Rule
rules.body: Gold appears only when real hardware is connected. No physical device exists for users yet, so in practice it is almost never seen.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: No uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrow or kicker labels. Section titles are Sora in sentence case; field labels are plain small text. Stored action names in capitals ("NEW TAB") are shown sentence-cased ("New tab") by `zoneLabel`; a mixed-case label the user typed is left alone.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Keys Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is for things you'd type or count. Never for headings or decoration.

rules.name: The No-Nest Rule
rules.body: A card never sits inside a card. Inside a surface, group with spacing and hairline rules.

rules.name: The Solid Material Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are opaque graphite. No glass, no blur, no colour on cards; the app's colour lives only in the frame, the wash and the app's own name and zones.

dos: Do put the app's colour only on the frame (`space-wash`), the page wash (`space-deep`), the app's name (`space-ink`), its icon plate and its trackpad zones.
Do use ink (`#ece8e1`) for the one primary action in a view; everything else is a graphite key or a quiet text action.
Do write section titles in Sora, sentence case, and field labels as plain 12px text.
Do draw the trackpad with `GlideZoneMap` at 600px (360px compact), mirrored left/right, lit from the swipe edge.
Do give every raised surface the inset top-light plus an offset drop shadow from the Shadow Vocabulary.
Do reuse the recipes in `lib/surfaces.ts` (CARD, GLASS_PANEL, KEYCAP_SHADOW, HERO_CARD, NOTICE_GLASS, BUTTON_*, FIELD_*) rather than hand-rolling a surface.
Do keep the logo mark at 1.56:1 with `object-contain`.
donts: Don't use the app's colour on buttons, charts, statuses or decoration.
Don't use violet for anything but Flow speaking, or gold for anything but real hardware contact.
Don't add uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrow or kicker labels.
Don't nest a card inside a card.
Don't use unicode glyphs as icons (arrows, checks, crosses, plus signs); use `icons.tsx`.
Don't scale the trackpad to fit its container or draw it at a third size.
Don't use glass, backdrop blur, glow, AI gradients or coloured shadows.
Don't fake 3D hardware or imply a connected device that doesn't exist.
Don't square-crop or circle-crop the logo mark.
